title: National Geographic double-blind remote viewing of the Dumbarton Bridge

tellings.quote: the end of the dumb Barton Bridge

plain: Joe McMoneagle, a man known for remote viewing, which is the practice of trying to describe a faraway place using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a test filmed for National Geographic in the San Francisco Bay Area. He says it was set up so that neither he nor the people with him knew the target, and that he described the end of the Dumbarton Bridge, which turned out to be where a man named Ed had gone. If true, it would suggest the mind can perceive distant places.
